name: Nithyakalyana Perumal Temple (Lakshmi Varaha), Thiruvidanthai
deity: Vishnu as Lakshmi Varaha, worshipped as Nithyakalyana Perumal, with Komalavalli Thayar
period: A Divya Desam of Thondai Nadu, sung by Thirumangai Alvar in thirteen verses of the Nalayira Divya Prabandham
summary: On the East Coast Road at Thiruvidanthai, Vishnu as Lakshmi Varaha is worshipped as Nithyakalyana Perumal, the Lord of the daily wedding — a Divya Desam of Thondai Nadu sung by Thirumangai Alvar.

sections.history: Thiruvidanthai is one of the 108 Divya Desams, the abodes of Vishnu sung by the Alvars in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham, and belongs to Thondai Nadu. Thirumangai Alvar praised the Lord of this village in thirteen verses. The temple is traditionally attributed to the Pallava age, in the seventh and eighth centuries, and a worn inscribed plaque within the precincts is said to place it in the eighth century. It was renovated under the Cholas in the eleventh century, and a Chola king, Vijaya Rajendra, is said to have granted the village to the temple. It stands on the East Coast Road in Chengalpattu district, south of Chennai.
sections.architecture: The sanctum is crowned by the Kalyana Vimanam, named for the wedding that gives the shrine its fame. The Lord is Lakshmi Varaha, Vishnu in his boar form, and Komalavalli Thayar has her own shrine. Two sacred tanks serve the temple, the Varaha Theertham and the Kalyana Theertham, and the sthala vriksha, the sacred tree, is the Punnai.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells of the sage Kalava, who had three hundred and sixty daughters. Vishnu came to the sage as a young brahmachari and married one daughter each day for a year, which is why he is called Nithyakalyana, the Lord of the daily wedding. At the end of the year, tradition holds, the daughters became one, honoured as Akhilavalli, the Goddess who is the whole of them. The temple therefore speaks of marriage as a sacred and continuing grace.
sections.festivals: Vaikunta Ekadashi and the annual Brahmotsavam are the principal festivals. Weddings and prayers for marriage also fill the temple on auspicious days. Confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: The temple has a special place for those praying for marriage. Devotees bring a garland, walk around the inner prakaram nine times and keep the garland at home; after the wedding, couples return it to the temple. Pause also before the Varaha image, and plan the visit along the East Coast Road, where the temple lies a short drive from Kovalam.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; Vaikunta Ekadashi and festival days are busiest. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: The temple is on the East Coast Road in Chengalpattu district, about 4 km from Kovalam (Covelong) and about 19 km south of Thiruvanmiyur in Chennai. Chennai is the nearest major airport, and the road from Chennai is the usual way; confirm bus connections locally.
